intro.eyebrow: The eastern gateway of the Silk Road
intro.title: Xi’an, Gateway to the Silk Road
intro.left: Known historically as Chang’an, Xi’an served as the capital of thirteen dynasties and the eastern starting point of the Silk Road. The city compresses centuries of Chinese history into a remarkably approachable stop, from Qin burial armies to Tang-era pagodas and a complete Ming city wall.
intro.right: Xi’an is not frozen in the past. You can spend the morning with the Terracotta Army, cycle above the old city in the afternoon, then follow food stalls and illuminated Tang-style streets after dark. Its compact center makes deep history easier to experience without the scale of Beijing.

plans.label: 3 days
plans.summary: Visit the Terracotta Army, walk or cycle the city wall, see the pagoda district, and explore the old city after dark.

plans.label: 4 days
plans.summary: Add the Shaanxi History Museum, quieter neighborhoods, and more time for local food without compressing the main sights.

plans.label: Extra day
plans.summary: Add Mount Hua or another cultural stop outside the city with private transfer support.

items.label: Getting there
items.summary: Xi’an is well connected by high-speed rail and has direct flights from many major Chinese cities.

items.label: Getting around
items.summary: The metro covers central sights; the Terracotta Army requires a separate transfer outside the city.

items.label: Where to stay
items.summary: Stay near the Bell Tower or inside the city wall for a compact first visit.

items.label: Planning ahead
items.summary: The Muslim Quarter is busiest at night. Explore beyond the main lane for a calmer and broader food experience.
